newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian rupee slips on late demand for dollar.
newsitem.headline: Indian rupee slips on late demand for dollar.

text.p: The Indian rupee slipped to 35.72/73 per dollar at close of trade on Friday after being range-bound at 35.685/695 for most of the day, dealers said.
The rupee traded at a high of 35.685 and a low of 35.73 during the day, they said.
"The rupee was steady at 35.685/695 for most of the day," a dealer at a foerign bank said. "But in the afternoon, there was some demand from a few banks which pushed the rupee down."
He said the dollar buying in the afternoon did not appear to be on account of corporate demand but was the result of banks covering short positions.
"Some banks seem to have been short...It was basically short-covering which pushed the rupee down," he said. "There is still no sign of the usual month-end demand."
A large state-run bank based in eastern India was one of the banks buying dollars in the afternoon, he said.
Dealers said the Reserve Bank of India bought dollars earlier in the day at between 35.69 and 35.695.
Premia on six-month forward dollars ended Friday steady at an annualised 9.35 percent, dealers said.
"There was both paying and receiving pressure during the day," a dealer at a state-run bank said. "But it was well-matched and there was no significant change in premia levels."
The forex market is inactive on Monday as banks are closed for local holidays in Bombay and some other centres.
